sections.h2: Who is responsible for each part of a Bay County bill?
sections.html:
The Bay County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, local governments set millage rates, and the Bay County Tax Collector prints, mails and collects the bill.

The Tax Collector's real estate page lays out the order. The appraiser assesses, the County Commission and other levying bodies set millage, the appraiser builds the roll, and the certified roll then moves to the Tax Collector. Any change to name, mailing address, location or assessed value has to go through the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector. Owners who pay through escrow should know the mortgage company requests the original bill and the owner gets a copy.

  • Property Appraiser: value questions and TRIM notice questions, (850) 248-8401, as printed on the Value Adjustment Board page.
  • Tax Collector: payment, delinquent tax and tax deferral.
  • Clerk of Court and Comptroller: official records, plus the clerk work for the Value Adjustment Board.

sections.h2: What is the yearly tax calendar in Bay County?
sections.html:
The yearly cycle tracks the Florida Department of Revenue calendar, and each step belongs to one office.

  • January 1: the date that fixes value and ownership for the tax year.
  • March 1: exemption and classification applications are due.
  • August: the Property Appraiser mails the TRIM notice of proposed taxes. A value challenge goes to the court clerk within 25 days of that notice.
  • September and October: taxing authorities hold tentative budget hearings, with final budget and millage hearings in October and November.
  • November: the Tax Collector sends the bill.
  • April 1: unpaid taxes become delinquent, and certificates are sold by June 1.

For a Bay County house listed in spring, that means the prior year's bill may still be open at closing while the new roll is being built.

sections.h2: Where are the Bay County Tax Collector's offices?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector lists four service offices, and a Bay County bill can only be paid at its own offices.

  • Panama City: 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, FL 32401.
  • Panama City Beach: 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, FL 32407.
  • Lynn Haven: 700 Florida Ave., Lynn Haven, FL 32444.
  • Callaway: 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy, Callaway, FL 32404.

Bring the property tax notice or the property address. Delinquent balances must be paid in certified funds, which the page lists as cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. Appointments can be booked through the Tax Collector's site, and online payment is offered too.

sections.h2: What does a Bay County seller do before listing?
sections.html:
Start with the tax notice and the Property Appraiser's record for the parcel, then compare the owner name to the deed. A name that does not match, or a mailing address that is out of date, means the bill may never reach you, and the Tax Collector's page says changes to name or address must be made through the Property Appraiser.

Next, check whether non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater or solid waste are on the bill, since those are billed beside the tax and are owed at closing like the rest. A house that sat vacant or was repaired after storm damage can have an assessed value that no longer matches its condition, which is a reason to review the TRIM notice in August rather than wait for the bill.

Finally, ask the title company for a lien and tax search. Panama City, Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway all sit in the same county tax system, so the same offices answer for any of them.

sections.h2: When are Bay County taxes due, and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Bills usually reach mailboxes by the first of November, the deadline is March 31, and April 1 starts delinquency. The discount months run November through February.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent off.
  • January: 2 percent off.
  • February: 1 percent off.

Non-ad valorem assessments, mainly paving, stormwater and solid waste collection, follow the same calendar and carry the same early payment discounts. They come from local governments and are certified to the Tax Collector, so a question about one goes to the government that levied it.

sections.h2: How do I file for homestead or other exemptions in Bay County?
sections.html:
Apply through the Bay County Property Appraiser before the March 1 cutoff, having made the home your permanent residence by January 1.

The Tax Collector's page is explicit that exemptions go through the Property Appraiser. State guidance prices the homestead exemption at up to $50,000: school taxes see only the first $25,000, while the second $25,000 reduces non-school levies on value above $50,000.

  • Save Our Homes keeps yearly assessed value growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is smaller, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • After a sale or foreclosure, the property is revalued at just value each following January.
  • A seller who rents the home out loses homestead, with a limited carve-out for servicemembers.

The Value Adjustment Board page adds that a timely filed homestead application that was denied needs no petition fee, while one received after March 1 does.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Bay County valuation?
sections.html:
Petition the Bay County Value Adjustment Board. The 2026 petition deadline fell on September 8, 2026, and the next filing window follows the TRIM notices mailed the following August.

Bay County Value Adjustment Board filing details as printed on its site
ItemDetail
Filing fee$50.00, non-refundable
Online filingAdds a 3.5% non-refundable card processing fee
Extra contiguous parcels or accounts$5.00 for each after the first
Mail address for checks225 McKenzie Avenue, Panama City, FL 32401

Section 194.014, quoted on that page, requires a petitioner contesting value to pay all non-ad valorem assessments and at least 75 percent of the ad valorem taxes, less the discount, before the taxes go delinquent. If the partial payment is missed, the board must deny the petition by April 20.

sections.h2: What can a Bay County owner do about a bill they cannot pay?
sections.html:
Florida offers a homestead tax deferral through Form DR-570, filed with the Tax Collector by March 31. It covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident aged 65 or older.

Section 197.222 of state law also allows an installment plan, with applications due May 1 of the assessment year. Ask the Bay County Tax Collector which plans it runs and what the payoff is.

Unpaid tax turns delinquent April 1, and state law requires certificates to be sold by June 1. Two years after April 1 of the issue year, the holder is allowed to seek a tax deed. A seller in that spot can usually settle the balance out of the price paid at the table.

sections.h2: What happens to Bay County tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on the roll receives the bill, and the year is divided between buyer and seller when the deal closes. Have the title company pull the current bill, any non-ad valorem balance and the discount month in effect.

A deed documentary stamp tax applies at 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, collected by the clerk at recording. Everyone named on a taxable deed is liable, even if the contract assigns payment to one side.

A buyer starts with no inherited cap once the next January arrives, so the seller's tax history is a poor guide to what the buyer will owe. Selling an inherited or storm-worn house works the same way: clear liens and unpaid balances first, then record the deed in Panama City.

faqs.q: What is the Bay County property tax due date?
faqs.a: March 31 is the due date, and April 1 starts delinquency. Notices normally go out by early November.

faqs.q: How much is the Bay County early payment discount?
faqs.a: Four percent in November, shrinking by a point each month through February, with nothing off in March.

faqs.q: Where is the Bay County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: Panama City is the central location, with additional offices in Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway. Bring your notice or property address.

faqs.q: Can I still file a 2026 value petition in Bay County?
faqs.a: The 2026 deadline was September 8, 2026, and later petitions are treated as late filed and reviewed. Questions go to the Property Appraiser at (850) 248-8401.

faqs.q: Does a Bay County buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. Ownership changes reset the property to just value the following January, with narrow exceptions such as some spousal transfers.
